analysis: All changed files are test-only under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Vision/. The changes are API-signature adaptations to an upstream mlx-swift-lm change: stub LanguageModel.prepare now takes (state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters) instead of windowSize (GLM5NextMediaRoutingTests.swift line 83; EngineV2VisionRoutingTests.swift line 129 per the patch). MediaIngest.decodeImage and decodeVideo results are now unwrapped through `.source` (MediaIngestTests.swift hunks at lines 118, 185, 209, 227, 533, 766). No production code, key handling, attestation, encryption, cache storage or authorization logic is modified. The EngineV2VisionRoutingTests excerpt (lines 1256-1695) is unchanged context. It exercises MediaError, noProcessedMedia and unsupportedMedia mapping to HTTP 400 with no refusal telemetry, cancellation mapping to 499 with the vision reservation released, and the fail-loud path for slots without a bridge. These tests assert existing fail-closed and availability behavior and do not weaken any control. Remaining integration question, outside the supplied evidence: the production MediaIngest wrapper type that now exposes `.source` and the new prepare/PrefillParameters protocol live in non-supplied files. I could not check whether they preserve the bounded-ingest, memory-backed video (T-050) and reservation semantics the tests assert. No new attack surface or threat-model gap is identified from these units.
